title: Front Squat
summary: A barbell squat with the bar on the front of the shoulders, so your torso stays upright and the quads do more.

equipment_needs.text: Needs: barbell (Olympic bar); weight plates; rack with J-hooks (power rack, squat stands or bench uprights).

muscles.why: Library rating 1 for quads (main mover): each working set adds 1 of a set to the weekly quads total.
Library rating 0.5 for glutes (helper): each working set adds 0.5 of a set to the weekly glutes total.
Library rating 0.5 for adductors (helper): each working set adds 0.5 of a set to the weekly adductors total.
Library rating 0.4 for upper back (helper): each working set adds 0.4 of a set to the weekly upper back total.
Library rating 0.2 for abs: below the counting floor, so it adds nothing to the weekly abs total.

setup.text: Rest the bar on your front shoulders, with your elbows high in a clean grip or with crossed arms.
Brace hard and keep your chest up.
Squat down as deep as you can while staying upright.
Stand back up, leading with your elbows.

form_cues.cue: Sit straight down with an upright torso
If your elbows drop, the bar will roll forward.

mistakes.text: Dropping the elbows so the bar rolls forward.

lower_risk.text: Warm-up: the app adds two or three ramp-up sets at rising loads before the first working set, unless that load is very light.
The app suggests a heavier load only when the jump is 5% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first.
Default target: 6-10 reps, stopping about 3 reps short of failure (RIR 3). Stop the set when form breaks down.
Use the same controlled range on every rep; lower under control rather than dropping or bouncing.
Set safety arms or pins where a missed rep can be set down, or use a spotter, and use collars.
Pick a variation and range you can train comfortably.
